RGB BA residual study: what reduces the ~0.84 px track residual AND improves the calibration, 2026-09-27
==========================================================================================================
Bag rec_20260924_204902 (night), 25 windows, protocol of tests/time_offset_eval_20260927.txt: final from the validated
zeroshot_pass2, halves A = windows[0::2] / B = windows[1::2] started from the variant's final, 1-sigma = |A-B|/sqrt(2)
(per camera, group medians), held-out = each half's calibration held on the other half with WHOLE tracks and no
variant option (a common yardstick), plane = median |landmark - LiDAR plane| of the final, shift = final vs the
validated final (/hdd/DM_calib/nt_regress/full/work/rgb/final = full/out) in units of the validated empirical 1-sigma
(floors 5 mm / 0.02 deg), > 3 sigma flagged. Work: /hdd/DM_calib/nt_regress/resid_study. Scripts: tests/resid_run_eval.sh,
tests/resid_compare.py (--bins), tests/resid_quick.sh, tests/resid_closure.py, tests/resid_retrack.py.

1. Variants (all config-gated; code in rgb/data.py, rgb/framecorr.py, rgb/obsweight.py, rgb/tracks_anchor.py)
   segN   rgb.solve.seg_span_s = N s: after the usual track selection (min_len, max 40 obs per track), every KLT track
          is cut into round(duration / N) equal-time pieces, each its own landmark. A landmark then only has to absorb
          the KLT drift of ~N s; the first board-free pass (design angles) keeps whole tracks.
   fc6    rgb.solve.frame_corr (rot + pos): 6-DoF correction of the LiDAR pose per synchronous camera frame (all 14
          cameras exposed together), fitted between stage-B rounds 1-2 with the landmarks/calibration held; prior
          0.2 deg / 20 mm, high-pass 1 s and zero mean per window (gauge vs the extrinsics), >= 3 cameras / 30 obs.
   fcr    as fc6, rotation only (quick subset only).
   agew   rgb.solve.obs_weight by age: empirical weights from the residual in |t - track centre| bins (per camera,
          5 quantile bins, floor 0.25, mean 1).
   kt     rgb.tracks.anchor: KLT with template-anchored re-measurement (key-frame template, re-anchor after 30 frames
          or on failure) instead of pure frame-to-frame LK (quick subset only; needs re-tracking).
   seg2fc seg2 + fc6.

2. Quick subset (2 windows S03 + W05, start = validated final, tests/resid_quick.sh; reproj median, px)
   q_base 0.795 | q_fc6 0.711 | q_fcr 0.725 | q_seg2 0.642 | q_kt 0.776 | q_agew 0.760
   Anchored tracking (kt), forward-backward closure on W05 (tests/resid_closure.py, px vs track age in frames):
     front5     f2f 0.08/0.15/0.21/0.25/0.27/0.53   anchored 0.14/0.30/0.46/0.60/0.71/0.70   (1-5/5-15/15-30/30-60/60-120/>120)
     side_left  f2f 0.12/0.23/0.35/0.50/0.68/0.83   anchored 0.19/0.36/0.55/0.73/0.89/1.38
     rear_left  f2f 0.03/0.11/0.18/0.31/0.58/3.66   anchored 0.11/0.22/0.36/0.66/1.40/7.93
   -> the anchored tracker drifts MORE (template appearance change at night, fisheye scale change) and costs ~3x the
      tracking CPU (20 jobs: 2546 cpu-s); residual gain only 0.795 -> 0.776. Dropped (anchor.enabled false).

     seg2fc speed 0.487/0.622/0.662/0.701/0.719  age 0.534/0.563/0.611/0.620/0.616  (rear 0.611/0.603/0.608/0.628/0.646)
   Per-frame correction (fc6) removes a residual share at every speed but leaves the growth with track age; splitting
   removes the growth with age (seg2: flat 0.62 -> 0.69 px instead of 0.68 -> 1.13 px); the speed dependence
   (trajectory) remains.

4. Reading
   - fc6: the per-frame trajectory error is real (residual 0.843 -> 0.764 px, the 0.36 px quadrature share of the
     residual-source analysis) but it is common to all cameras of a frame, zero-mean per window, and already averaged
     out by the extrinsics: half-split 1-sigma, held-out and plane distance are unchanged. Lower residual, no
     calibration gain -> off.
   - agew: down-weighting old observations helps neither 1-sigma nor held-out -> off.
   - kt: section 2 -> off.
   - segN: the KLT drift is not white noise: a whole track's drift (0.3-0.5 px over 2-4 s front, several px rear) is
     absorbed by ONE landmark, so it biases the extrinsics in a direction set by the windows' motion, i.e. differently
     for halves A and B. Cutting tracks into ~2 s pieces keeps each landmark's drift sub-pixel while keeping enough
     baseline (at >= 3 m/s, >= 6 m) for depth. Result: half-split 1-sigma falls sharply where the drift is worst
     (rear position 31.5 -> 6.3 mm, rear axis 15.6 -> 2.5 mm, rear rotation 0.25 -> 0.08 deg, rear f 0.98 -> 0.62 px;
     front+top axis 7.6 -> 2.4 mm, position 13.8 -> 7.7 mm), the landmarks sit closer to the LiDAR planes
     (rear 35 -> 24 mm), held-out on whole tracks is unchanged (0.848 vs 0.849: the calibration explains unsplit
     tracks as well as before) and no camera moves more than 1.15 sigma from the validated result (median 2.7 mm;
     the largest shift, rear_left 22 mm, is inside the validated rear 1-sigma of 31-39 mm). Side stays within noise
     (2 cameras, one split: rot 0.042 -> 0.045 deg, axis 3.7 -> 4.2 mm, position 8.3 -> 7.1 mm).
   - seg1 vs seg2 vs seg3: 1 s pieces are best for the front cluster (axis 2.2 mm, f 0.23 px) but worse for the side
     axis (6.4 mm) and rear (13.3 / 9.2 mm) - the shorter baseline weakens depth for the lateral cameras - and moves
     the result more (max 1.79 sigma, median 5.6 mm); 3 s leaves half the drift (rear axis 4.9 mm). 2 s is the best
     balance: best or near-best in every group, no bias.
   - seg2fc: frame corrections on top of seg2 lower the residual further (0.671 -> 0.592 px; corrections 33/17/8 mdeg
     rms about LiDAR x/y/z, 2.3-3.2 mm) but the calibration hardly moves (vs seg2 final: max 1.03 sigma, median 2.0 mm)
     and 1-sigma is the same within the one-split noise: front+top axis 2.4 -> 2.8 mm, rear 6.3/2.5 -> 5.9/2.4 mm, side
     axis 4.2 -> 2.1 mm (both side cameras 3.7/4.7 -> 1.7/2.4 mm, but fc6 alone moved them 1.5/5.9 -> 3.7/3.5 mm, i.e.
     inconsistently). Not enough evidence for the extra per-frame state; stays off (a candidate to re-test on a
     second bag, especially for the side cameras).
   - Caveat: 1-sigma comes from ONE half split per variant (per camera a single |A-B| sample); group medians over
     10 / 2 / 2 cameras. Side (2 cameras) differences of +-1-2 mm are noise.

5. Pipeline path (rgb.solve.seg_span_s: 2.0 applies to zero-shot pass 2 and the final, not pass 1)
   zero-shot pass 2 with seg2 from the validated pass 1 (5 windows): reproj 0.899 -> 0.713 px, extrinsics within
   2-14 mm / 0.01-0.09 deg of the validated pass 2 (wall 492 vs 372 s, loaded box). Final (25 windows) from it: reproj 0.6705 px, plane 25.9 mm, every camera within
   0.0-1.4 mm / 0.000-0.005 deg of seg2_final (max 0.27 of seg2's 1-sigma; vs the validated result max 1.17 sigma,
   rear_left 22.9 mm / rear_right 16.9 mm, all others <= 4.1 mm / 0.03 deg). The pass-2 start does not matter.
   Wall 38 min / RSS 9.4 GB (shared box, next to another agent's pipeline run).

6. Decision
   rgb.solve.seg_span_s: 2.0 is the new default (README section 10); the validation held-out is measured on whole
   tracks without the study options (pipeline._val_rgb_tasks) so it stays comparable. frame_corr, obs_weight and
   tracks.anchor stay off. The accuracy gain is from ONE bag and one half split per variant: re-check the side/rear
   1-sigma on the next bag (tests/resid_run_eval.sh, set seg_span_s in the fragment).
